2.

sentences.text: The petitioners are accused A16 and A41, who have filed a petition under Section 227 of Cr.P.C to discharge them from the charges levelled against them under Sections 120(B), 420, 465, 468, 471 and 409 of IPC.

The respondent police has filed a charge sheet against 41 accused persons, including the petitioners on the allegation that they also conspired with the other accused, especially with A1 to A6, had swindled hefty amount of money from the Bank by furnishing false documents in their names.
3.As per the case of prosecution, the petitioners have applied for Housing Loan with Punjab National Bank by showing false address at Trichy.
It is alleged that the petitioners are actually the residents of Theni District and that is evidenced from their Aadhar Card.
The petitioners https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on: 16/07/2025 12:38:30 pm ) income also did not match to their loan applied by them and eventually the loan was also sanctioned to them.

4. The loan amount of Rs.46 lakhs was recommended by A3, Thiyagarajan and sanctioned by A2,
Durga Madhavan on 18.06.2016.
The process note was prepared by Chitra Lakshmi.

The details of the loan amount sanctioned to the petitioners on various dates has been given on the following table:
Sl. Name of Accused & Branch & Date Loan amount States of Disbursement No Loan A/c No. of sanction in Rs.

Kovil Street, 21.06.2016 - Rs.3,47,000/- 361800NC000415 Trichy  21.06.2016 - Rs.17,01,200/-
20.06.2016 14.10.2016 - Rs.17,00,000/-
18.04.2017  Rs.5,00,000/-
2 M.Ramesh (A41) PNB, Trichy  Rs.46 lakhs 06.10.2016  Rs.34,28,000/-
A/c.No. 30.09.2016 06.10.2016 - Rs.4,70,000/- 437300NC00000480 13.10.2016 - Rs.34,28,000/-
13.10.2016 - Rs.34,28,396/-
03.11.2016  Rs.6,61,928/-
5.The allegation is that even without raising any construction the loan, which has been transferred to the account of these accused have been retransferred to the account of A1 and thus, the public funds were swindled by all the accused.
K.Pitchaimani vs The State Of Tamil Nadu on 9 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/99318768/
2 https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis
6.The learned counsel for the petitioners submitted that the petitioners are not the beneficiaries and they are just the victims to the criminal conspiracy of the other accused.

These petitioners have entered into those transactions by believing that the transactions are genuine and later, came to understand that the properties registered to them had already been registered in favour of someone's name and they have been cheated.

7.The learned Special Public Prosecutor appearing for the respondent submitted that the petitioners are fully aware of what is being done on to their accounts and only with their connivance, the amount has been retransferred to the account of A1.
He further submitted that the amount has been sanctioned in one lot, which is against the principle of disbursing the building loan in stages.

8.The records also would show that the whole of the building loan has been sanctioned at one stretch, even without verifying whether the building has been actually constructed and whether it has reached each stage for release of the loan at each stage.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis
9.In fact, the petitioners are the permanent residents of Theni District, as per their Aadhar Cards.
But they have applied loan to Punjab National Bank, Trichy, for which, no explanation is given.
Even for some extraneous reasons, the petitioners had opted to apply loan in the Trichy Branch, then they could have shown their original address itself.

10.It is the allegation of the prosecution that the petitioners have managed to furnish some false address in Trichy, in order to show that they are the residents of Trichy, who fall within the predominent service jurisdiction area of Trichy.
11.It is also seen that some of the consent letters given in the name of the petitioners are forged.
When the petitioners are aware that the loan amount was being transferred to their account, they would have been aware of the fact that someone has given consent letter in their names.
12.Even for any reasons, the petitioners have been misused by someone and they are just victims.

Those facts cannot be known to them even before the petitioners have been subjected to trial.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on: 16/07/2025 12:38:30 pm )

13.As of now, there are enough materials to frame charges against these petitioners also for the offence under Sections 120(B), 420, 465, 468, 471 and 409 of IPC and it is not a case, where these petitioners have been roped in the case without any materials.

As the Courts are not expected to make any rowing enquiry about the merits of the evidence and materials and that exercise can be done only at the time of trial and also considering the serious allegations and the modus operandi alleged to have been adopted by the accused, learned trial Judge thought it fit to dismiss the application.
